purpose: Cited residue, nitrogen, energy and emission-factor references for the Today view residue income, energy footprint and carbon footprint blocks (TODAY_ECONOMICS_FOOTPRINT_SPEC section 5). Regional references, not measurements of any field.

conventions.units: kg, tonnes, MJ/kg, m3, INR; N rates kg N/ha; methane factors kg CH4/ha/day; N2O EF in kg N2O-N per kg N.
conventions.residueBasis: rpr is residue mass per unit of product mass in the productBasis form, as the source reports it. The IISc atlas does not state a moisture basis (its method paper speaks of sun-dry residue); treat as approximately air-dry, not oven-dry.
conventions.derivedValues: Where a source prints generation, production and surplus but not the ratio, rpr and surplusFraction are derived by division and the derivation is recorded on the figure.
conventions.nulls: A missing value means no cited figure was found; it never means zero.

gwp100.note: CH4 non-fossil (biogenic; rice and residue burning). CH4-fossil is 29.8. Uncertainties are the printed +/- values (5-95% range); the engine uses the central values.

biomassCarbonFraction.note: IPCC default C content of above-ground crop residues (0.42 kg C/kg dm). The 0.47 value is the herbaceous-biomass carbon fraction for grassland, not a crop-residue value.

riceMethaneBaselineKgPerHaDay.locator: Table 5.11 (Updated), p5.53, regional row South Asia, 95% interval
riceMethaneBaselineKgPerHaDay.note: India lies in the IPCC South Asia region, so the regional default is used; the world default is kept under world. Baseline = continuously flooded, no organic amendment, non-flooded pre-season < 180 days.

riceWaterRegimeScaling.locator: Table 5.12 (Updated), disaggregated case unless named aggregated; page image checked

ricePreSeasonWaterScaling.note: SFp, the water regime before the season. Separate from the straw amendment factor below.

none.note: SFo = 1 with no organic amendment (Equation 5.3 with ROA = 0)

ricePreSeasonStrawScaling.equation: SFo = (1 + ROA x CFOA)^0.59, ROA = straw applied in t dry matter/ha
ricePreSeasonStrawScaling.note: IPCC gives no fixed straw scaling factor: SFo depends on the straw rate. low/high are null because computing them needs an ROA, which code must take from the field (e.g. residue x share incorporated). Straw left on the surface or burnt does not count (Table 5.14 note a).

n2oEf1.note: Aggregated default low is 0.002 (not 0.001). Wet climate = tropical annual rainfall > 1000 mm.

residueBurning.locator: Table 2.5 (Agricultural residues row), Table 2.6 (post harvest field burning)
residueBurning.note: Table 2.5 prints no SD for the agricultural-residue CH4 and N2O factors. Table 2.6 lists combustion factors only for wheat, maize, rice and sugarcane residues; other crops have none. CO2 from burning crop residue is not reported (assumed balanced by regrowth).

dieselKgCo2PerLitre.locator: Section on three-wheeler factors, Step 2 (PDF p27)
dieselKgCo2PerLitre.note: Indian programme figure for diesel combustion CO2 per litre (consultation version 1.0, 2015). CO2 only.

dieselKgCo2PerTJ.locator: Table 3.3.1, off-road mobile sources, Diesel, Agriculture (PDF p36)
dieselKgCo2PerTJ.note: IPCC default for agricultural machinery; per-litre use needs a cited diesel energy content.

ureaManufactureKgCo2ePerKgN.locator: Plant paragraphs: Yara Babrala 0.43 (lowest), Mangalore Chemicals and Fertilisers 1.13 (highest; naphtha and furnace oil)
ureaManufactureKgCo2ePerKgN.boundary: Production stage at the plant (CSE Green Rating Project, three-year plant averages to about 2017); CO2 only. Field use and N2O are excluded. Upstream gas supply and transport are not stated as included, and whether the CO2 bound into urea is netted out is not stated.
ureaManufactureKgCo2ePerKgN.derivation: kg CO2 per kg N = (t CO2 per t urea) / 0.4664, where 0.4664 = 28.01/60.06 is the nitrogen mass fraction of urea CO(NH2)2 by formula. 0.43/0.4664 = 0.92; 1.13/0.4664 = 2.42.
ureaManufactureKgCo2ePerKgN.note: Plant range, not an India average. Read from Down To Earth (the CSE magazine) reporting the CSE rating; the CSE report "Grain by Grain" itself was not retrieved. Urea N only; DAP and complex fertilisers are not covered.

lpgMjPerKg.note: IPCC default NET calorific value. The paddy straw value is a GROSS (bomb) value, so LPG equivalents of straw energy are overstated by the gross-net gap (not quantified here). No Indian official LPG calorific value was retrieved.

dieselMjPerLitre.locator: IPCC Table 1.2 Gas/Diesel Oil NCV 43.0 MJ/kg x HPCL BS-VI density at 15 C 810.0-845.0 kg/m3
dieselMjPerLitre.derivation: 43.0 MJ/kg x 0.810 kg/l = 34.83 MJ/l (low); 43.0 x 0.845 = 36.34 (high); value = 43.0 x 0.8275 (midpoint of the density specification) = 35.58. The midpoint is an arithmetic choice, not a measured density.
dieselMjPerLitre.note: Net calorific value per litre from an IPCC default and an Indian BS-VI product specification range; actual density of a given lot is not known.

dieselDensityKgPerLitre.locator: HSD-BS-VI Specifications, item 3 Density at 15 C (IS 1448 P:16)
dieselDensityKgPerLitre.note: Specification limits, not a measured average.

dieselMjPerKg.note: IPCC default net calorific value per kg.

methaneKgPerM3.note: IPCC conversion factor of m3 CH4 to kg CH4 (the reference temperature is not printed beside it).

cbgMethaneShare.note: CBG under IS 16087:2016 is described as more than 90% methane; 0.90 is the floor. Search summaries mention a later revision with a 95% minimum, which was not retrieved.

biogasM3PerTonneDm.locator: IITD abstract (187 L biogas and 85 L CH4 per kg VS, untreated straw) x IITG Table 1 (rice straw VS 78.26% of TS)
biogasM3PerTonneDm.derivation: 187 m3/t VS x 0.7826 t VS/t TS = 146.3 m3 biogas per t dry matter; 85 x 0.7826 = 66.5 m3 CH4 per t dry matter; methane share 85/187 = 0.455.
biogasM3PerTonneDm.note: Cross-study derivation: the yield is IIT Delhi laboratory digestion of untreated paddy straw; the VS share is rice straw collected near Guwahati (IIT Guwahati). Laboratory specific yield, not a plant figure; pretreated straw yielded 500 m3 biogas per t VS. Dry matter here means total solids.

uses.label: Biomass for compressed biogas
uses.priceBasis: Paddy straw bought from balers for the Farm Gas CBG plant, Ghungreli, Ludhiana, Punjab; previous season (2023) procurement, reported 30 Jan 2024; moisture basis not stated
uses.note: Punjab price, not Karnataka or Tamil Nadu; as-traded (baled, moist) tonnes, not dry matter.

uses.label: Fuel for a biomass power plant
uses.priceBasis: Rs 169 per quintal offered by biomass power plants, Muktsar, Punjab, 2024 season (report of 19 Sep 2024); delivery point and moisture basis not stated
uses.note: Converted Rs 169/quintal x 10 = Rs 1,690/tonne. Plants state their own cost as Rs 300/quintal including operations; that is not a farmer price.

uses.label: Dry fodder for cattle
uses.priceBasis: Stored paddy straw sold by farmers, Karnal, Haryana, December 2023: Rs 250/quintal (parmal) to Rs 300/quintal (basmati); moisture basis and delivery point not stated
uses.locator: paragraph with the quintal prices; Deputy Director Agriculture quote
uses.note: Converted x 10 to Rs/tonne. The buyers named include gaushalas (cattle), buyers in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi, IOCL Panipat and other industries, so this is a general straw market price in a fodder-deficit trade, not a fodder-only price. Haryana, not Karnataka or Tamil Nadu. The DES by-product value per hectare (byProductValueInrPerHa) is the official KA and TN farm value of straw but carries no quantity.

notes: Husk (ratio 0.20 of production, surplus 0.60 KA) is a mill by-product and is not listed as a field residue use.

biogasM3PerTonneVs.note: Laboratory specific yield per tonne of volatile solids for untreated straw (pretreated straw reached 500 m3 biogas and 266 m3 CH4 per t VS). Methane share 85/187 = 0.45. The per-tonne-dry-matter figure in biogasM3PerTonneDm combines this with the IITG VS share.

carbonFraction.note: Carbon 38.8% of paddy straw briquettes (as tested). Recorded beside the IPCC 0.42 default; not used by the engine unless the orchestrator decides so.
